decisions.executionNote: Begin a gradual elbow-continuous right-arm approach above the ruler; keep left arm parked and gripper open.
Continue rotating the right gripper toward a downward grasp while approaching the ruler's right half above the surface.
Continue the overhead approach in small orientation increments, maintaining the current elbow branch.
Move over the ruler's right section while completing the downward wrist turn; keep fingers clear of blocks.
Finish positioning over the ruler without contact; monitor the right wrist and keep the left arm stationary.
Bring the open jaws vertically above the ruler's right section, completing the down-facing orientation before descent.
Match jaw yaw to the ruler and descend cautiously toward its sides; table height and fingertip offset remain visually estimated.
Close the right jaws around the ruler's right section at low height; grasp retention will be checked by the ruler's visible motion.
Turn the held set square flat in the tabletop plane to make its long pushing edge horizontal; check that it follows the jaws.
The ruler visibly follows the grasp. Slide its straight edge forward at constant height, correcting the remaining slight yaw to collect the blocks without lifting.
Continue a slow level push so all three blocks seat against the straight edge; the middle block still needs to square up.
All three blocks now appear square and aligned. Draw the ruler back slightly, then release it on the table before resetting the arm.
Lift the open gripper clear of the released ruler, preserving the aligned row; begin a safe retreat for reset.
Reset along a smooth reverse wrist rotation and backward path, keeping both arms on their current elbow branches and clear of the completed row.
Continue returning the open right gripper toward its initial pose; the released ruler and aligned blocks remain undisturbed.
Continue the smooth right-arm reset, retracting within its own workspace with the gripper open.
Continue controlled retraction toward the initial right-arm pose, preserving elbow continuity and the aligned row.
Approach the home pose gradually with the open right hand; avoid any further contact with the ruler or blocks.
Slow the final home approach and correct the small left-arm drift; maintain a continuous elbow configuration as both hands reset.
